body.p: In view of the claim amendments below remarks, the Examiner is respectfully requested to reconsider the rejections.
Office Action Summary

Support for this amendment is found within Applicant's filed specification at least at page 6, lines 16-24, page 7, lines 19-23, FIG. 1, and FIG. 3B.

Gillian paragraph [0093] describes "At 608, a radar feature indicative of a characteristic of the target is extracted from the radar data. The radar feature may provide a real-time measurement of the characteristic of the target, position of the target, or dynamics of the target. The radar feature may include any suitable type of feature, such as a detection feature, reflection feature, motion feature, position feature, or shape feature, examples of which are described herein. In the context of the present example, reflection radar features and motion radar features of the user's hand are extracted from the radar data."
Gillian paragraph [0073] describes "As another example, consider a scenario in which

the signal transformer 502 transforms the raw radar data into a measure of the target object's velocity over time. In turn, the feature abstractor 504 uses this information to identify a finger fast-tap motion by using a threshold value to compare the target object's velocity of acceleration to the threshold value, a slow-tap feature, and so forth. Any suitable type of algorithm can be used to extract a feature, such as machine-learning algorithms implemented by a machine-learning component (not shown) of the digital signal processor 126."

Gillian paragraph [0077] describes "The user detection application 524 may detect, based on sensor data or radar data, presence of a user. In some cases, the user detection application 524 also tracks the user when the user is detected in the environment. For example, the user detection application 524 may detect the presence based on a detection radar feature 512 and shape radar feature 520 that matches a known 3D profile of the user. The user detection application 524 can also verify detection of the user through image data provided by the RGB sensor 220 or voice data provided by the acoustic sensors 212."

Gillian paragraph [0078] describes "In some embodiments, the activity detection application 526 uses the sensor data and the radar data to detect activity in the computing device 102's environment. The activity detection application 526 may monitor radar for detection features 512 and motion features 516. Alternately or additionally, the activity detection application 526 can use the acoustic sensors 212 to detect noise, and the RGB sensor 220 or depth sensor 224 to monitor movement."

The Examiner stated on page 4 of the Office Action, regarding claim 16, that Gillian at the above-referenced excerpts ([0093], [0073], [0077], [0078]) describes "providing the pseudo sensor data derived based on at least the machine learning model to an application to enable the application to process the pseudo sensor data and native sensor data to enable tracking the activity of the user." The Examiner applies the same rationale to reject the corresponding aspect of independent claim 27 (Office Action, page 17) and independent claim 35 (Office Action, page 24).
However, Gillian does not disclose or suggest the aspect as amended, or providing, using

the first apparatus comprising the radio frequency based tracker, the pseudo sensor data derived based on at least the machine learning model to a second apparatus comprising an application to enable the application to process the pseudo sensor data and native sensor data to enable tracking the activity of the user, the first apparatus being different from the second apparatus, and the first aparatus being separate from the second apparatus other than with a wireless connection.

The functionality described in the above-referenced paragraphs of Gillian ([0093], [0073], [0077], [0078]) is described with reference to Gillian FIG. 5. Refer for example to Gillian paragraph [0077] ("the user detection application 524 may detect the presence based on a detection radar feature 512 and shape radar feature 520 that matches a known 3D profile of the user"). In Gillian, the sensor fusion engine 110 includes the feature abstractor 504 (which includes detection 512 and shape 520), and the sensor fusion engine 110 is connected to the sensor-based applications 108 that includes user detection 524. However, the sensor fusion engine 110 and the sensor-based applications 108 are all within the same device, or the computing device 102. Refer to FIG. 1, where the computing device 102 includes sensor fusion engine 110 and sensor-based applications 108, such that the sensor fusion engine 110 and the sensor-based applications are software within the computing device 102. The sensor-based applications 108 and sensor fusion engine 110 are not apparatuses.

2. Dependent Claim 22

It is respectfully submitted that the prior art does not disclose or suggest "performing at least one of: docking, using the first apparatus, the second apparatus, or charging, using the first apparatus, the second apparatus, wherein the first apparatus comprising the radio frequency based tracker provides the pseudo sensor data during the time interval when the first apparatus is docking
the second apparatus or when the first apparatus is charging the second apparatus." Support for this amendment is found within the filed specification at page 11, lines 35-38 and FIG. 4.
3. Dependent Claimn 34

It is respectfully submitted that the prior art does not disclose or suggest "receive, with the apparatus comprising the radio frequency based tracker from the another apparatus comprising the application with a wireless signal, an explicit indication that the another apparatus comprising the application is not providing the native sensor data, or to track the user; and provide, with the apparatus comprising the radio frequency based tracker, the pseudo sensor data in response to receiving, from the another apparatus comprising the application with the wireless signal, the explicit indication that the another apparatus comprising the application is not providing the native sensor data, or to track the user." Support for this amendment is found within the filed specification at page 8, lines 16-17 ("the gap may be defined by a message or trigger signal indicating that the sensor 399 is not able to generate sensor data") and page 8, line 38 to page 12, line 2 ("the health and fitness tracker 104 may trigger the RF based tracker 110 to track the user in response to the health and fitness tracker 104 transmitting an indication, such as by transmitting a trigger signal or sending a message, to the RF based tracker 110").
4. Even if it was obvious to combine the references, they do not disclose or suggest all of the elements/features of the claims, as explained above

Applicant respectfully traverses the rationale to combine the references to support a rejection under Section 103. For example, in Stivoric the transmitting device (sensor or accelerometer) transmitting the data fails, whereas in Applicant's case the receiving device (user equipment 104) receiving the pseudo sensor data is failing to provide native sensor data for itself: the receiver (the user equipment 104) fails to provide the native sensor data, which is why the RF based tracker 110 provides the pseudo-sensor data. Therefore, one skilled in the art would not be motivated to combine Gillian with Stivoric to arrive at Applicant's claimed invention. Even if, for the sake of argument, it was obvious to combine the references, they do not disclose or suggest all of the elements/features of the claims, as explained above.
5. Other dependent claims

Though the other dependent claims contain their own allowable subject matter, these claims should at least be allowable due to their dependence from allowable independent claims. However, to expedite prosecution at this time, no further comment will be made.

The Applicant respectfully requests the Examiner enter this amendment and pass the claims to issue. The undersigned representative welcomes the opportunity to resolve any matters that may remain, formal or otherwise, via teleconference at the Examiner's discretion.
